builder_plan.scenario: A workflow needs specialist review, but extra agents may add more cost than useful work.
builder_plan.change: Test the proposed division of work against a single-agent implementation.
builder_plan.baseline: One agent with the same tools and an equal total token and time budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted outputs, coordination failures, wall-clock time, and total cost across all agents.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SciMARS: Multi-Agent Recursive Self-Improvement for Closed-Loop Scientific Discovery
summary: It replaces a fixed multi-agent team with static roles, handoffs, and memory policies by adding a shared evidence graph plus separate editors that rewrite roles, coordination, and memory policies between attempts, selected via candidate probes. The cost is substantial orchestration complexity, additional API calls for the editing and probe steps per task attempt, and a shared graph that must be maintained and kept coherent. It can fail when editors propagate erroneous self-modifications, when the underlying model is weaker (GLM-5.3 results show near-zero benefit), and when the evaluation setting (experimental-data replay, digital twin) does not transfer to real closed-loop lab work.
rationale: The approach runs on third-party APIs and is within constrained infrastructure, but the model-dependent gains, heavy harness complexity, and replay-based evaluation require workload-specific validation before production adoption.
technique: Self-adapting multi-agent harness with shared evidence graph

claims.statement: It replaces a fixed multi-agent team with static roles, handoffs, and memory policies by adding a shared evidence graph plus separate editors that rewrite roles, coordination, and memory policies between attempts, selected via candidate probes. The cost is substantial orchestration complexity, additional API calls for the editing and probe steps per task attempt, and a shared graph that must be maintained and kept coherent. It can fail when editors propagate erroneous self-modifications, when the underlying model is weaker (GLM-5.3 results show near-zero benefit), and when the evaluation setting (experimental-data replay, digital twin) does not transfer to real closed-loop lab work.

Resolves 12/18 vs 8/18 base-team attempts on Autonomous Science Bench (GPT-6-Astra), 14/38 vs 11/38 on ScienceAgentBench, and 11/20 vs 5/20 on AppWorld; gains are inconsistent across models (2/18 vs 1/18 for GLM-5.3).
